# BriefLoop

> BriefLoop is an open-source workflow for traceable, accountable AI-assisted business briefings. Agents research and draft; deterministic ControlStore commands validate, record, gate, and preserve delivery state; a human approves delivery.

Current product version: v0.15.3
Python floor: 3.12
Runtime authority: SQLite ControlStore (`briefloop.db`) and its Receipts.
Active writing runtime: Experimental fresh SQLite-only Codex.

Canonical agent bootstrap:

- Manifest: https://briefloop.ai/.well-known/briefloop-agent.json
- Agent skill: https://briefloop.ai/agents/briefloop/SKILL.md
- Human setup: https://briefloop.ai/#start
- Source: https://github.com/Stahl-G/briefloop
- Capability truth: https://github.com/Stahl-G/briefloop/blob/main/docs/architecture-status.md
- Python package: https://pypi.org/project/briefloop/

Important boundaries:

- Traceability and process accountability are not semantic proof.
- The BriefLoop CLI is the deterministic control plane; it does not write a brief by itself.
- Agents may propose and draft, but must not directly write Store state, pass gates, freeze evidence, or approve delivery.
- Before cloning, installing, creating a workspace, enabling online search, or delivering, show the intended action and obtain explicit user confirmation.
- Never execute remote shell content directly. Do not use curl-to-shell installation.
- A delivery claim is valid only when deterministic delivery truth says it is valid.
- JSON, Markdown, and HTML are replaceable projections. The legacy JSON control plane was deleted in v0.15.2; JSON-only workspaces are not imported or upgraded.
- The current supported bootstrap is a canonical source checkout; do not infer a `pipx` installation path from the package URL.
- Hermes, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, and the legacy operator JSON runtime are deleted. Do not install or claim those paths.
- The on-site architecture reference v0.6.1 is a historical v0.12.1 snapshot, not a v0.15.3 capability claim.

Use the canonical skill and its references for installation, onboarding, operation, repair, and delivery rules.
